Let the number have digits a and b with a + b = 13 and a − b = 3 (since 9(a − b) = 27).

Then a = 8 and b = 5, so the number is 85 and its reversal is 58. Check: 85 − 58 = 27 ✓.

The sum is 85 + 58 = 143. In general this equals 11(a + b) = 11 · 13 = 143.

Solution 1 uses a wrong pair (7,4), whose digits sum to 11, not 13. Solution 2 makes an algebra error. Solution 3 is correct.

CHOICE: 3
